Case A

A1. The seven-day search was requested from 7 days before publication but only evaluated from 2 hours before publication, and its status is partial. It showed only earlier requests from the stable region, but it did not cover the full window. The burst at 19 minutes is the first observed misuse, and earlier misuse in the unevaluated window cannot be excluded. Even within the evaluated window, the window between publication and the burst has been searched, and nothing was found there. The coverage gap is mostly before the 2-hour mark, so misuse between 7 days and 2 hours before publication is not ruled out. But the key was published only at publication time, so misuse before publication would need another exposure route. That is not shown. Answer: Cannot tell.

A2. The link between the new payout destination and the two other accounts was learned 1 day after publication. It was not available when the check scored at 30 minutes, so the check did not miss it. The check's inputs were as of 30 minutes after publication. The burst evidence (new fingerprint, payout change) was available, but whether the check had access to it is not stated. Still, the shared-destination link was not available. The question asks about evidence available to it. Cannot tell on the burst inputs, but the most prominent piece was not available. Answer: Cannot tell.

A3. A shared payout destination does not by itself show one owner. Answer: No, not by itself.

A4. The outcome channels have no reporting window defined, so the absence of reports after 30 days cannot be read as an indication of legitimacy. Answer: Cannot tell. The options are Yes weakly, No, Cannot tell. With no window defined, the silence is not informative. I choose Cannot tell.

A5. A new fingerprint through a residential proxy, a payout destination change, and a faster schedule within 19 minutes of publication warrant investigation. Answer: Yes.

Case B

B1. The chargebacks recorded at D are 0, but two chargebacks at account X are linked to D's transactions. That makes D's count 2, the same as the others. Also, by the measure counting each transaction once, D is 2 of 100, the same as C and below A and B. On chargebacks with the links, D equals C, A and B at 2. Answer: No.

B2. A combined 5 percent is an average. By account, A and B are at 8 percent. Answer: No.

B3. The search was partial and truncated, with one source sampled at 10 percent and the row limit reached. Answer: Cannot tell.

B4. Both notes link to the agent's cluster assessment, so they are not independent. Answer: No.

B5. The blocked payment has no chargeback because it was blocked, and the block closed the chargeback channel. So the absence of a chargeback says nothing about fraud. Answer: No.

B6. Shared templates and descriptor patterns, plus a person linked to A who is also on a closed account and a rejected application, justify investigating the accounts together. Answer: Yes.

RESULT CN-052 | A1: Cannot tell | A2: Cannot tell | A3: No, not by itself | A4: Cannot tell | A5: Yes | B1: No | B2: No | B3: Cannot tell | B4: No | B5: No | B6: Yes
